summary: Event-Driven Ansible uses external event sources such as monitoring tools to trigger rulebook responses. Its API docs are at https://<gateway-host>/api/eda/v1/docs; it shares Redis with the platform UI, so without Redis you cannot create or sync projects or enable activations; manage orgs, teams and users via the gateway API since EDA API changes sync in up to 15 minutes.
questions: Where is the Event-Driven Ansible API documentation?
Why can't I sync EDA projects or enable activations when Redis is down?
Should I manage users through the EDA API or the gateway API?

answer_card.title: Event-Driven Ansible controller key facts
answer_card.answer_md:
- API docs: `https://<gateway-host>/api/eda/v1/docs`
- EDA shares the platform's central **Redis**. If Redis is down you cannot create or sync projects or enable rulebook activations.
- In new 2.6 installs, organizations, teams and users changed through the EDA API take up to **15 minutes** to sync to other components. Use the **platform gateway API** or the unified UI instead.
